messages:
maria (Support): FYI customer on Dedicated seeing 503s and token throttles. They say it spikes when their long-context summarization jobs run for ~30s per request. Started ~09:10 UTC. :ambulance:
jamal (Eng Runtime): Thanks — tenant id? model? concurrency? any repro so we can correlate with KV eviction metrics? :eyes:
maria (Support): Tenant acct-993. Model: longformer-32k variant. Concurrency ~6, burst to 18. They provided logs — past 20m shows repeated kv evict waves and then request throttling.
infra-oncall-bot: Alert: ded-prod-kv-pool-3 high eviction rate for tenant=acct-993 (evict_rate>900/s) at 2024-07-21T09:12:03Z
ellen (Support Eng): Can you paste the tail of the logs here? curious about fragmentation messages and any OOMs. Also did autoscale trigger?
maria (Support): pasted snippets below (redacted tokens, kept raw lines):
```
[2024-07-21T09:11:58Z] evict: tenant=acct-993 kv_used=92.3% kv_free=7.7% evict_rate=1152/s
[2024-07-21T09:12:01Z] kv_fragment: tenant=acct-993 frag_ratio=0.68 free_chunks=312
[2024-07-21T09:12:05Z] throttle: tenant=acct-993 reason=kv_pressure fallback=rate_limit 503
[2024-07-21T09:12:10Z] autoscaler: pool=ded-prod-kv-pool-3 decision=scale_up reason=behind_by_2_reqs
[2024-07-21T09:12:25Z] evict: tenant=acct-993 kv_used=94.7% evict_rate=1305/s
[2024-07-21T09:12:40Z] request: id=req-7a9 throttle=1
```
ellen (Support Eng): Noted. Autoscaler attempted to scale but there's often a delay before new hosts join + warm KV state. That fits an eviction wave causing tail latency + 503s.
ajmal (Eng Runtime): Two immediate asks: 1) can we reproduce locally with a tenant-local repro harness? 2) capture kv stats across ded hosts during the wave (kv_used, fragment ratio, free_chunks, evict_rate, gc_ops).
maria (Support): Customer willing to run a repro. They said a single long request (32k tokens) + steady concurrency causes it. Provided this command they run in prod: 
```bash
support-repro --tenant acct-993 --model longformer-32k --seq 32768 --concurrency 8 --rps 6 --duration 600
```
alex (Infra): Looks like fragmentation is high (frag_ratio=0.68). When fragmentation + high kv_used combine, eviction ends up doing a lot more work per freed byte. That can blow past eviction throttles and trigger global per-tenant rate limits.
ellen (Support Eng): Repro steps I recommend for us to run in staging (safe):
1) run the support-repro above against a dedicated staging pool with tenant quotas
2) tail kv metrics using: 
```bash
./metrics-tail --hosts ded-stg-kv-pool-2 --filters tenant=acct-993 --metrics kv_used,evict_rate,frag_ratio,free_chunks,gc_ops --interval 1s
```
3) if we hit eviction wave, capture host-level `free_chunks` distribution and `kv_compaction` logs

jamal (Eng Runtime): If repro matches, immediate mitigation options: temporarily bump tenant's kv_quota/memory or enable per-tenant aggressive compaction (experimental). Longer term: reduce cold-warm join penalty by seeding KV caches on scale events.
maria (Support): Customer asked about billing impact / why rate-limited vs queued. They saw successful requests later but cost spiked. Any guidance for customer message?
alex (Infra): Explain that throttle is protective (prevents full pool destabilization) — we can offer a short-term reserved burst or increase dedicated capacity. Also offer to run a canary repro to show reduced failure rate after changing config.
ellen (Support Eng): I'll coordinate a staged repro with customer and we can try: (A) bump tenant kv_memory by 20% for 30m, (B) enable aggressive compaction on pool-3, (C) run repro and collect metrics.
maria (Support): Customer agreed to a 30m bump. They've given a redacted auth token for repro: `redacted:****`. I'll schedule a 09:45 UTC repro slot.
jamal (Eng Runtime): One more note: check per-host kernel scheduler bursts — long-context jobs can cause head-of-line KV locks if we do large single-threaded IO. If we see per-host stall logs like `kv_lock_wait>200ms` that's a smoking gun.
ellen (Support Eng): Copy. I'll start the staging repro and paste results here. If we confirm fragmentation + slow warmup, plan is: short-term kv_memory bump + trigger compaction, medium-term seeding on scale-up, long-term avoid single-request huge seqs without prefetching KV blocks.
maria (Support): Thanks team. I'll update customer with the mitigation plan and confirm after 09:45 run. :thumbsup:
